ActorTypesInput.description:
The actor types the request declares; the envelope writes them only as
`declared_unverified`, and Access's bindings win (P-12).

evidence.description: One per evidence presenter, in `evidence` order.

on_behalf_of.description: One per `on_behalf_of` ring, in chain order.

ApprovalAnswer.description: A request pushed to the Approval Surface.

expires_at.description: When the surface stops showing it, RFC 3339.

ApprovalReturned.description: What the approval return hands back.

claim.description:
The approver's `authentication` Claim Access put on the redirect, its `ClaimID` as
unpadded base64url of 16 bytes; the next authority request sends it as
`proofs[].claim_ref` when the first answer was `next: step_up`.

contribution.description:
The contribution `ExerciseID` Access confirmed, unpadded base64url of 32 bytes; the next
authority request sends it as `proofs[].contribution`.

ledger.description: The ledger, `led_…`, the next authority request names.

next.description:
What the caller does next: `commit`, a new authority request with the contribution, and
the Claim when there is one, as its proofs, whose allowed Exercise the Declaration write
then refers to.

render_digest.description:
The digest of the render the approver approved, unpadded base64url of 32 bytes; the
caller compares it with the render it computes itself.

AuthContextAnswer.description:
The Access authentication context an unsigned human record names; not an author signature
(P-21 item 3).

digest.description: Access's digest of the artifact, lower-case hex.

AuthContextInput.description: The Access `auth_context` artifact of an unsigned human record.

artifact.description: The tagged `COSE_Sign1` as Access issued it, unpadded base64url.

digest.description: Access's `digest` of it, unpadded base64url of 32 bytes.

exercise.description: The allowed `ExerciseID`, unpadded base64url of 32 bytes.

next.description:
What the caller does next: `step_up` when Access also asks for the approver's fresh
authentication, which the passkey assertion on the Approval Surface meets beside the
approval, so the new request sends the returned Claim as `claim_ref` beside the
contribution; `approve` to have the request approved on the Approval Surface and send a
new request with the contribution as its proof.

receipt.description:
The decision receipt `COSE_Sign1` exactly as Access signed it, unpadded base64url; a
record's `authority` digest is its SHA-256.

step_up.description: The authentication terms among them, verbatim.

unmet.description: The unmet terms, as Access shows them to the requester.

AuthorityInput.description: The Access Exercise the record's `authority` refers to.

intent.description: The canonical intent envelope Access allowed it for, unpadded base64url.

pos.description: The position that last changed it.

ChangesAnswer.description: One page of the Works that changed after a cursor (P-57, T-26).

changes.description: The Works, in the order of the position that last changed them.

more.description: True when more changes follow at once.

next_cursor.description: The cursor to ask with next, `cur_…`.

position.description: The positions the answer reflects, `pos_…` (T-97 item 2).

resync.description:
True when the cursor no longer opens a difference: read every Work again; nothing is
missing silently.

CheckpointAnswer.description: A checkpoint of the ledger's transparency log.

issued_at.description: When it was issued, RFC 3339 UTC.

CompromiseWindowAnswer.description:
A compromise window the record falls in (SEC-36 item 4): derived from the notice the Work
service Party wrote for an Access compromise declaration, never part of the record (C-4).

window_to.description: The window's end, the declaration's commit time, RFC 3339 UTC.

EvidenceAnswer.description:
A record's evidence, each kind apart (P-20): an author signature, the ledger's acceptance,
the inclusion proof and the external time and witnesses are never shown as one another.

oneOf.description: The Access authentication context of an unsigned human record.

proofs.description: The approvals the commit relies on.

get.description:
The `redirect_uri` Work sends to the Approval Surface. Access puts the contribution Exercise,
the render digest and Work's `state` on the redirect; the caller's client hands the query to
this route with its own token. The `state` must be the one Work issued for this caller's
pushed request, unused and unexpired, and is used up by an answer; the contribution must be
an Exercise Access allowed in the caller's realm's domain, asked of Access now. The answer is
the contribution the caller sends as the proof of its next authority request, whose allowed
Exercise the Declaration write refers to. Work approves nothing here.

post.description:
Work's PEP commits the caller's intent at Access's decision point under the Actor Intent
Statement the caller's own device signed; Work signs nothing for the caller and approves
nothing. The intent must be the `work:commit` of this existing ledger, valid now, and the
statement must name exactly this commit, Work's PEP and the domain of the caller's realm. An
allowed Exercise is answered only with its decision receipt verified for the intent and
addressed to Work's PEP. When Access asks for more, the answer says what: a step-up at
Access, verbatim from Access's terms, or an approval on Access's Approval Surface, with the
typed request and, given the approver's contribution, the pushed request's URL. A denial is
`403`; when Access cannot be asked, nothing is answered as authority.

post.description:
The record is admitted only under the Access Exercise its `authority` refers to: Access is
asked for that Exercise on every request, its decision receipt must verify and be exactly the
proof the `authority` digest names, the intent must be `work:commit` on this ledger and valid
now, and the record's capacity must be the Exercise's. A signed record is checked against the
key Access binds at admission; an unsigned one must be the caller's own, with its Access
`auth_context`. When Access cannot be asked, nothing is written.
